explanation: Leaf yellowing is a common initial manifestation of BLB chlorotic halos.
Water-soaked wavy marginal lesions are pathognomonic for BLB infection.
Bacterial ooze droplets confirm active Xanthomonas vascular exudate.
Cloudy bacterial streaming in water test confirms vascular bacterial blight.
Uniform browning/yellowing strictly on bottom leaves indicates N deficiency not BLB.
Inward leaf tube rolling indicates drought stress not BLB.
Explicit absence of leaf lesions rules out Bacterial Leaf Blight.
Chlorosis is the primary symptom of nitrogen deficiency.
Nitrogen remobilization strictly affects lowest older leaves first.
Soil nitrogen depletion occurs uniformly across entire field/soil zones.
Presence of discrete wavy lesions indicates pathogen infection not nitrogen deficiency.
Bacterial streaming rules out pure abiotic nutrient deficiency.
Inward leaf rolling is a classic physiological drought avoidance mechanism.
Symptom reversal within 24h of watering confirms moisture stress.
Presence of wavy lesions indicates bacterial pathogen infection not moisture deficit.
